title: Find starboard
prompt: You’re standing at the console of the Mako, facing the bow. Starboard is…
explain: Starboard is the right side when you face forward, on a boat or a plane. Matt checked it in the Guidebook on his first flight; Josh and Ben already knew.

field.title: Port and starboard drill
field.do: On your next car ride, bike ride or walk, call “starboard!” for every right turn and “port!” for every left, the whole way. Then teach it to someone in your family.
field.need: Any trip, and someone to teach
field.log: Who you taught, and the trick you used to remember it. (“Port” and “left” both have four letters.)

title: Rig the poles
prompt: Dan rigs eight poles the night Matt arrives. Put the rig in order from the rod tip down.
explain: Main line to a swivel so the line doesn’t twist, a small weight to get the bait down, a short heavier leader that gill plates and oysters can’t cut, then the lure.

field.title: Rig a practice line
field.do: Rig a line the way Dan does, from the tip down: main line, swivel, weight, leader, then a paper clip where the hook would go. Tie the line to the swivel with a uni knot.
field.need: Fishing line or string, a swivel or key ring, a sinker or washer, a paper clip
field.log: Draw your rig from top to bottom and label every piece.

link.label: How to tie the uni knot

title: Read the water
prompt: The Mako drifts over a seagrass bed. Which fish should you expect, and with what?
options: Seatrout, on a yellow feather tipped with shrimp
Snook, deep under the mangrove roots
Redfish, popping cork over an oyster bar
explain: “Grass bed fishing meant trout.” Mangroves and oysters hold snook and reds; deep holes hold grouper.

field.title: Read real water
field.do: Spend ten minutes reading a pond, creek, canal or beach without fishing it. Where is it shallow? Deep? Moving? Shady? Where are the logs, docks, rocks and weeds? Pick the spot you would cast first, and say why.
field.need: Any water you can safely stand beside
field.home: Look at a lake near you on a satellite map with a grown-up and find the same things from above.
field.log: Sketch the water and mark your three fishiest spots with an X.

title: Pick the tide
prompt: Matt wants water over the oyster bars at South Point and bait moving along the mangroves. When does Dan say to fish?
options: The hour either side of high tide
explain: Fish the hour either side of the high. A ‘morning high’ means plenty of water over the bars.

field.title: Plan the tide three days running
field.do: Look up today’s high tide at Chokoloskee and write down Dan’s fishing window: the hour either side of the high. Do it three days in a row and watch how the time moves.
field.log: Three days of high-tide times and your fishing window for each.

title: Log the night meeting
prompt: Two boats and a car meet in the dark at South Point. Matt hears one name. Write it in the log.
explain: “Rawley.” The grocery-store owner. Keep that name; it matters in Chapter 20.

field.title: Stakeout notes
field.do: Pick one spot (a porch, a window, a park bench) and watch for fifteen minutes like Matt at South Point. Write down everything that comes and goes, with the time: cars, people, birds, dogs, boats.
field.need: A watch or clock, your journal
field.log: Your stakeout log, with times. Circle the one thing a detective would ask about.

title: Revive the snook
prompt: The 36-inch snook is beside the boat and tired. Put the release in order.
items: Hold it upright in the water
Move it gently back and forth so water passes over the gills
Wait for the tail to kick on its own
Open your hands and let it swim
explain: Snook are closed season in summer and go back every time. Matt did exactly this, and earned the first badge.

field.title: Learn the release by heart
field.do: Say the four release steps from memory, then teach them to a grown-up. Add the rule good guides use: wet your hands before you touch a fish you’re letting go. Next time you fish, do it for real.
field.log: The four steps in your own words, plus the wet-hands rule.

title: Name the fish in the cooler
prompt: The Rabbit Key cooler holds trout, redfish, snapper and one rare one. Tap the black drum.
explain: Deep-bodied, gray-black, chin barbels, vertical bars when young. ‘Hard to find these days,’ Dan says.

field.title: Fish detective
field.do: At a grocery fish counter, a bait shop or an aquarium, find three fish and name them by body shape, fins, mouth and markings before you read the label. Then check the label.
field.need: A fish counter, bait shop or aquarium
field.home: Play Fish ID on Hard, then draw one fish from memory.
field.log: Sketch one fish and label the three clues you used.

title: Which snake?
prompt: A snake swims toward the lantern at Comer Key. How can you tell a cottonmouth from a harmless water snake while it swims?
options: A cottonmouth swims with its whole body on the surface
explain: Cottonmouths float high with the whole body on top; harmless water snakes swim with just the head up. The white mouth gape is a warning, not an attack.

field.title: Make a wildlife card
field.do: With a grown-up, find out which venomous snakes live where you live (your state wildlife agency or the library will know). Make a pocket card with their names and the rule: give every snake room, never touch, back away slowly.
field.log: Copy your card into the journal.

title: Plot the drop
prompt: A seaplane lands without lights and flashes three times. Which key?
explain: Pavilion Key, before dawn. Snapper poles the Mako into the mangroves so nobody hears a motor.

field.title: Make a treasure map
field.do: Draw a map of your yard, block or park with a compass rose (find north with a compass or a phone), three landmarks and an X. Hide something small at the X and see if someone can find it using only your map.
field.need: Paper, a compass or phone compass, a small “treasure”
field.log: Your map, and how long it took them to find the treasure.

link.label: The real chart from the book

title: Decode the call
prompt: Dan’s voice on the phone: “Trust me. Head to Lostman’s River in the Sea Belle.” Which channel, and when?
explain: Channel 16 is the international hailing and distress channel. Dan says to leave it open from nine to ten at night.

field.title: Radio check
field.do: Learn three radio words: “over” (your turn), “roger” (I heard you) and “mayday” (life in danger). Practice a radio call with someone in another room, or with walkie-talkies. Then make sure you know the real one on land: call 911.
field.need: A partner; walkie-talkies if you have them
field.log: Write the mayday call you would make from the Sea Belle: boat name, where you are, what’s wrong, how many aboard.

title: Provision the Sea Belle
prompt: A week of solid eating for two goes aboard at Everglades Marina. Which of these did Dan’s list definitely include?
options: Peanut butter and three loaves of bread
Nothing, they planned to catch it all
explain: Peanut butter, three loaves, cereal, cans, meat, milk, eggs, butter. Plus donuts, which are power food.

field.title: Provision a trip
field.do: Plan the food for a three-day fishing trip for two, with no fridge after the first day. Write the list, check what’s already in your kitchen, and help with the real shopping if you can.
field.log: Your list, with a star next to the power food.

title: Tie off for the storm
prompt: The squall drives the Sea Belle onto an oyster bar. Secure the houseboat in order.
items: Run a bow rope to a solid mangrove
Set the stern anchor out behind
Get aboard and wait it out
explain: Bow to the mangrove, stern anchor out: the boat ‘stretched secure from end to end.’ Then don’t swim back through a ghost net.

field.title: Make a storm plan
field.do: With your family, make a storm plan: how you’d know one is coming (watch the sky, check the forecast), where you’d go, what you’d bring. Learn the rule: when thunder roars, go indoors.
field.log: Your family’s storm plan, signed by everyone.

title: Why the gator came
prompt: An alligator takes half of Snapper’s grouper at the Sea Belle. What drew it in?
options: The splashing of a hooked fish
explain: Splashing says ‘something is hurt here.’ Matt’s rule about not splashing is real guide wisdom.

field.title: Sit still, count wildlife
field.do: At a pond, creek or park with a grown-up, sit still and quiet for ten minutes and count every animal you see: birds, turtles, fish, frogs, bugs. Notice what makes them leave. Where alligators might live, stay well back from the water’s edge.
field.log: Your count, and what scared things off.

title: Size the unseen giant
prompt: Something drags the anchored Bonefisher across the channel before the line snaps. Snapper’s guess?
options: A grouper, three hundred pounds or more
explain: A goliath grouper in a deep hole between the islands. Dan’s line: there is such a thing as too much fish.

field.title: Size it up
field.do: Guides size a fish by eye. Guess the length of five things (your bed, your arm span, a table, a bike, a dog), then measure them. Then mark Matt’s 36-inch snook on the floor with tape and lie down next to it.
field.log: Your guesses, the real numbers, and how close you got.

title: The Everglades choir
prompt: Matt lies awake on deck listening. Which sound is NOT part of the choir?
explain: Mullet, frogs, birds. No roads for twenty miles.

field.title: Your own choir
field.do: At dusk, lie outside or by an open window for five minutes with your eyes closed and count every separate sound. Sort them: nature or people.
field.log: Your list of sounds, and which ones you’d hear at Lostman’s River.

title: The dolphin and the shark
prompt: Matt is cutting a calf free of a ghost net when a hammerhead arrives. The mother dolphin rams the shark. Why?
options: Because sharks and dolphins always fight
She mistook it for a fish
explain: Dolphin mothers defend calves hard, and dolphins have been seen ramming sharks. Then she bit the last strand of net herself.

field.title: Clean up a ghost net
field.do: With a grown-up and gloves, pick up fishing line, hooks and trash at a pond, beach or park. Count the pieces of fishing line: lost line traps birds and turtles the way the ghost net trapped the calf.
field.log: What you found, and how many pieces of line.

title: Close the cut
prompt: Doc is bleeding ‘like a dang amberjack’ and talks Matt through it. Put the steps in order.
items: Stitch it with needle and thread
explain: ‘Just sew me up like two pieces of clothes.’ Matt’s first stitches.

field.title: Check the first-aid kit
field.do: With a grown-up, find (or build) a first-aid kit for the car, the boat or a backpack. Check it has bandages, gauze, tape, antiseptic wipes and gloves. Learn the first rule for a bad cut: press hard on it with something clean and get a grown-up.
field.need: A first-aid kit, or the things to make one
field.log: Your kit checklist, with what you added.

title: Float her off
prompt: The Sea Belle is stuck on the bar. Which tide gets her off?
options: The 9 a.m. high tide, with Doc towing and the boys pushing
Low tide, when the bar is dry
Any tide if you push hard enough
explain: Wait for the water to come back. Push and pull on the morning high, and mind the propeller.

field.title: Float her off
field.do: Put a toy boat “aground” on a rock in a pan or tub. Add water a cup at a time until she floats free. Then try pushing her off with less water. Which works better, the tide or the shove?
field.need: A pan or tub, a toy boat, a rock, a measuring cup
field.log: How many cups it took, and what happened when you pushed.

title: Old Scarface
prompt: Ninety minutes, and Old Scarface is on the deck. Weigh him in for the tournament, or put him back?
explain: Matt let him go. ‘Tough call. Good call,’ said Snapper. Either way, you earned the tarpon badge for landing him.

field.title: Your fishing day
field.do: Go fishing with a grown-up: a pier, a pond, a dock, anywhere. Use everything: rig, read the water, pick the time, and release anything you’re not keeping the right way. Check the fishing rules for where you go with your grown-up first.
field.home: Casting practice: tie a practice plug (no hook) on a rod, put a hula hoop twenty feet away, and make ten casts. Count the ones that land inside.
field.log: Date, place, what you caught (or your casting score), and your best moment.

title: Name the informant
prompt: Three clues: the name at South Point, the drop at Pavilion Key, the call on channel 16. Who is the FBI’s informant?
explain: Uncle Dan. Rawley was the undercover agent, the real smugglers are in jail, and the cargo was sunken treasure.

field.title: Interview a captain
field.do: Interview a grown-up who has fished or has a good story. Ask five questions: your first fish? your biggest? worst weather you were ever out in? best advice? a story you’ve never told me? Matt learned the truth by listening.
field.log: Their five answers.

title: Follow the money
prompt: Matt gets a share of a $20,000 reward. What does he try to do with it?
options: Keep it in a Dorito bag forever
explain: He offers it to Doc, and Rose walks in with the trophy having already done the same.

field.title: Pay it forward
field.do: This week, do one thing for someone else without being asked, the way Matt and Rose both tried to help Doc.
field.log: What you did, and what happened.

title: The airboat
prompt: Dad’s red airboat, restored. What lets it run on inches of water?
options: Nothing hangs below the hull; a caged propeller above the stern pushes it
explain: No prop or rudder in the water, so it slides over grass and mud. Loud, no brakes, and it needs a license, hence the DMV.

field.title: Build a shallow-water boat
field.do: Build two boats out of foil: one with a deep, narrow hull and one flat and wide like an airboat. Float each in a tub and load pennies until it sinks. Which carries more?
field.need: Foil, a tub of water, pennies
field.log: Pennies each boat held, and a sketch of the winner.

title: Sign the Guidebook
prompt: Dad’s name, then Matt’s, then two blank lines. Sign yours.
explain: ‘Dad always said we were in it together.’ Your license is ready to print.

field.title: Write your page
field.do: Write one page for the next assistant guide: the three most important things you learned this summer. Sign it under Dad’s and Matt’s names, then hand your journal to the grown-up who signed your missions for the last sign-off.
field.log: Your page for the next assistant guide.
